governedCriteria.observation: I opened both original production PNGs and saw the blue focus ring in both. The Avalonia perimeter probe matched the blue sample on 192 of 192 pixels.
Neither inspected PNG shows a black default focus adorner. The native perimeter probe recorded zero unexpected dark pixels.
Both inspected captures show the Check tag label in the unchecked appearance. The archived real checkpoint is focused and unchecked following pointer and keyboard interaction.
The recorded before-focus, after-focus and after-toggle geometry is identical per platform: Web 0,136,87.625,24 CSS px; Avalonia 24,136,96,24 DIP. This does not establish intermediate-frame geometry.

observations: Read-only inspection opened both original rendered PNGs of official PR #1128 run 45116325567, job 137499900958, artifact dotnet-package-conformance-failure.

Official capture used GitHub PR #1128 merge commit 71ab9f3e4f80feefbd6412e4e9110962b90c4ff4; CheckTag Web and Avalonia PNG bytes are byte-identical to tracked artifacts, and candidate 540503b63d1fdd03d2c1627b8a1d256d77402aad only deduplicates markdown-runtime error rendering.
Web artifact is an 88x24 CheckTag element crop; Avalonia artifact is a 960x720 full window. Both tracked PNG bytes equal the inspected original PNGs.
Nine functional observations pass in both executions; timing is diagnostic only.
limitations: Only the light/default/zh-CN/ltr/reduced-motion CheckTag checkpoint was independently accepted, not full CI, AOT, package, cross-platform rendering equivalence or performance.
Three recorded bounds checkpoints do not prove absence of intermediate-frame movement; cross-platform clocks were not synchronized.
AT-SPI and the Orca process are not spoken-output evidence. NVDA and VoiceOver were not tested. The Web CheckTag PNG is an element crop, not a visual inspection of the whole viewport.
